summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos pair a common gadget or robot with a surprising 'it doesn't see/hear/feel what you think' hook, like the gyro robot, clap switch and IR robot. Generic 'How does X work?' titles and very new posts do poorly, and the soil sensor video got almost no views but 24 shares, so it has potential.
winningPattern: Instagram-first Hindi Reels about a relatable robot or sensor (gyro, clap switch, IR, DHT11, mic) with a myth-busting hook: 'X doesn't do Y, it only does Z'. Short Hinglish titles with one emoji, a visible robot or demo, and a clear surprise in the first second. Saves and shares come from 'aha' explanations and robot demos, not from plain 'how does it work' questions.
doMore: Use the 'doesn't see/hear/feel, only does Z' hook on every video
Feature robots and the clap switch: they get the most saves and shares
Post Instagram first and keep Hindi titles in Hinglish
Make follow-ups to winners, such as a clap switch part 3 and gyro robot variants
Test the soil sensor topic again with a stronger visual, since its shares were high (24) but views low
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles with no surprise
Posting on YouTube only, which gets near-zero reach
Near-duplicate topics (smoke detector, IR darkness, automatic tap) that split the audience
nextTopics: Line follower robot failure on a black table
